sanskrit: yadā moham anuprāptaḥ sasvedaś ca janārdanaḥ tatas tān prāyaśaḥ pārtho vajrāstreṇa nijaghnivān
english: When Janārdana himself had fallen into a daze and was bathed in sweat, then Pārtha slew the most of them with the weapon of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: śataśaḥ pāṇayaś chinnāḥ seṣujyātalakārmukāḥ ketavo vājinaḥ sūtā rathinaś cāpatan kṣitau
english: By the hundreds their hands were severed, still gripping arrows, bowstrings, hand-guards and bows; standards, horses, charioteers, and warriors fell to the earth.

sanskrit: drumācalāgrāmbudharaiḥ samarūpāḥ sukalpitāḥ hatārohāḥ kṣitau petur dvipāḥ pārthaśarāhatāḥ
english: Like trees, like mountain peaks, like rain-clouds in form, the well-caparisoned elephants, their riders slain, fell to the ground, struck down by Pārtha's shafts.

sanskrit: vipraviddhakuthāvalgāś chinnabhāṇḍāḥ parāsavaḥ sārohās turagāḥ petur mathitāḥ pārthamārgaṇaiḥ
english: Their saddle-cloths and reins flung apart, their trappings cut, their lives gone, the horses fell with their riders, mangled by Pārtha's arrows.

sanskrit: sarṣṭicarmāsinakharāḥ samudgaraparaśvadhāḥ saṃchinnā bāhavaḥ petur nṛṇāṃ bhallaiḥ kirīṭinā
english: Sundered by the Diademed One's broad-headed shafts, the arms of men fell to earth still holding spears, shields, swords, nails, maces, and battle-axes.

sanskrit: bālādityāmbujendūnāṃ tulyarūpāṇi māriṣa saṃchinnāny arjunaśaraiḥ śirāṃsy urvīṃ prapedire
english: O lord, heads like the rising sun, like lotuses, like the moon in their beauty, severed by Arjuna's arrows, came to rest upon the earth.

sanskrit: jajvālālaṃkṛtaiḥ senā patribhiḥ prāṇabhojanaiḥ nānāliṅgais tadāmitrān kruddhe nighnati phalgune
english: When the wrathful Phalguna struck down his foes, the host blazed with his ornamented, life-devouring, many-marked feathered shafts.

sanskrit: kṣobhayantaṃ tadā senāṃ dviradaṃ nalinīm iva dhanaṃjayaṃ bhūtagaṇāḥ sādhu sādhv ity apūjayan
english: As Dhanaṃjaya churned the army like an elephant churning a lotus-pond, the hosts of spirits honored him, crying "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tat karma pārthasya vāsavasyeva mādhavaḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā talam āhatya pūjayat
english: Seeing that deed of Pārtha's, worthy of Vāsava himself, Mādhava fell into the utmost wonder and, clapping his hand, paid him homage.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃśaptakān hatvā bhūyiṣṭhaṃ ye vyavasthitāḥ bhagadattāya yāhīti pārthaḥ kṛṣṇam acodayat
english: Then, having slain most of the Saṃśaptakas who had stood their ground, Pārtha urged Kṛṣṇa on, saying, "Drive toward Bhagadatta."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yiyāsatas tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pārthasyāśvān manojavān apraiṣīd dhemasaṃchannān droṇānīkāya pāṇḍurān
english: Saṃjaya said: As Pārtha wished to set out, Kṛṣṇa then urged on his white steeds, swift as thought and decked in gold, toward Droṇa's array.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ kuruśreṣṭhaṃ svāṃs trātuṃ droṇatāpitān suśarmā bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ yuddhārthī pṛṣṭhato 'nvayāt
english: As that best of the Kurus set forth to save his own folk, who were sorely pressed by Droṇa, Suśarman, eager for battle, followed at his back together with his brothers.

sanskrit: tataḥ śvetahayaḥ kṛṣṇam abravīd ajitaṃ jayaḥ eṣa māṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ suśarmāhvayate 'cyuta
english: Then he of the white horses, the unvanquished victor, said to Kṛṣṇa: "O Acyuta, here is Suśarman, with his brothers, challenging me."

sanskrit: dīryate cottareṇaitat sainyaṃ naḥ śatrusūdana dvaidhībhūtaṃ mano me 'dya kṛtaṃ saṃśaptakair idam
english: "And in the north there our host is being rent asunder, O slayer of foes; today these Saṃśaptakas have made my mind divided in two."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu saṃśaptakān hanmi svān rakṣāmy ahitārditān iti me tvaṃ mataṃ vettha tatra kiṃ sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: "Shall I slay the Saṃśaptakas, or shall I guard my own who are afflicted by the foe? You know my thought in this — which course would be the right one?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dāśārhaḥ syandanaṃ pratyavartayat yena trigartādhipatiḥ pāṇḍavaṃ samupāhvayat
english: Thus addressed, the Dāśārha turned the chariot back to where the lord of the Trigartas was summoning the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ suśarmāṇaṃ viddhvā saptabhir āśugaiḥ dhvajaṃ dhanuś cāsya tathā kṣurābhyāṃ samakṛntata
english: Then Arjuna, having pierced Suśarman with seven swift arrows, cut down his standard and his bow with two razor-edged shafts.

sanskrit: trigartādhipateś cāpi bhrātaraṃ ṣaḍbhir āyasaiḥ sāśvaṃ sasūtaṃ tvaritaḥ pārthaḥ praiṣīd yamakṣayam
english: And the brother of the Trigarta lord, together with his horses and his charioteer, Pārtha swiftly dispatched to Yama's abode with six iron shafts.

sanskrit: tato bhujagasaṃkāśāṃ suśarmā śaktim āyasīm cikṣepārjunam ādiśya vāsudevāya tomaram
english: Then Suśarman hurled at Arjuna an iron lance resembling a serpent, and at Vāsudeva a javelin.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ tribhiḥ śaraiś chittvā tomaraṃ tribhir arjunaḥ suśarmāṇaṃ śaravrātair mohayitvā nyavartata
english: Arjuna cut the lance apart with three arrows and the javelin with three, and having stunned Suśarman with a volley of shafts, he turned away.

sanskrit: taṃ vāsavam ivāyāntaṃ bhūrivarṣaśaraughiṇam rājaṃs tāvakasainyānāṃ nograṃ kaś cid avārayat
english: O king, as he advanced like Vāsava, pouring forth a flooding rain of arrows, not one fierce warrior of your host could stay him.

sanskrit: tato dhanaṃjayo bāṇais tata eva mahārathān āyād vinighnan kauravyān dahan kakṣam ivānalaḥ
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya pressed forward, slaying the great car-warriors of the Kurus with his arrows, as a fire consumes dry brushwood.

sanskrit: tasya vegam asahyaṃ tu kuntīputrasya dhīmataḥ nāśaknuvaṃs te saṃsoḍhuṃ sparśam agner iva prajāḥ
english: The irresistible onslaught of that wise son of Kuntī they could no more endure than living creatures can endure the touch of fire.

sanskrit: saṃveṣṭayann anīkāni śaravarṣeṇa pāṇḍavaḥ suparṇapātavad rājann āyāt prāgjyotiṣaṃ prati
english: Enveloping the ranks with a downpour of arrows, the son of Pāṇḍu, O king, swept on toward the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa with the swoop of Suparṇa.

sanskrit: yat tadānāmayaj jiṣṇur bharatānām apāyinām dhanuḥ kṣemakaraṃ saṃkhye dviṣatām aśruvardhanam
english: That bow which the victorious Jiṣṇu now drew — a bringer of safety in battle to the fleeing Bharatas, and a multiplier of the tears of foes —

sanskrit: tad eva tava putrasya rājan durdyūtadevinaḥ kṛte kṣatravināśāya dhanur āyacchad arjunaḥ
english: that very bow, O king, did Arjuna bend for the destruction of the warrior class, all on account of your son, that gambler at the wicked dice.

sanskrit: tathā vikṣobhyamāṇā sā pārthena tava vāhinī vyadīryata mahārāja naur ivāsādya parvatam
english: Thus shaken by Pārtha, your army was rent asunder, great king, like a boat that has struck against a mountain.

sanskrit: tato daśa sahasrāṇi nyavartanta dhanuṣmatām matiṃ kṛtvā raṇe kruddhā vīrā jayaparājaye
english: Then ten thousand bowmen turned back, heroes resolved in their wrath upon either victory or defeat in the fight.

sanskrit: vyapetahṛdayatrāsa āpaddharmātigo rathaḥ ārchat pārtho guruṃ bhāraṃ sarvabhārasaho yudhi
english: His heart free of fear, that car-warrior — who in the law of dire need surpassed all others — Pārtha, who could bear every burden, took upon himself a heavy load in the battle.

sanskrit: yathā naḍavanaṃ kruddhaḥ prabhinnaḥ ṣaṣṭihāyanaḥ mṛdnīyāt tadvad āyastaḥ pārtho 'mṛdnāc camūṃ tava
english: As a rutting elephant of sixty years in its fury would trample a thicket of reeds, so did Pārtha, straining at his utmost, trample your host.

sanskrit: tasmin pramathite sainye bhagadatto narādhipaḥ tena nāgena sahasā dhanaṃjayam upādravat
english: When that army had been thus crushed, King Bhagadatta on that elephant rushed all at once upon Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: taṃ rathena naravyāghraḥ pratyagṛhṇād abhītavat sa saṃnipātas tumulo babhūva rathanāgayoḥ
english: That tiger among men received him fearlessly with his chariot, and tumultuous was the clash between the car and the elephant.

sanskrit: kalpitābhyāṃ yathāśāstraṃ rathena ca gajena ca saṃgrāme ceratur vīrau bhagadattadhanaṃjayau
english: Each equipped according to the rules of warfare — the one with his chariot, the other with his elephant — the two heroes, Bhagadatta and Dhanaṃjaya, ranged about in the battle.

sanskrit: tato jīmūtasaṃkāśān nāgād indra ivābhibhūḥ abhyavarṣac charaugheṇa bhagadatto dhanaṃjayam
english: Then, from his elephant huge as a thundercloud, Bhagadatta, overpowering like Indra, rained a flood of arrows upon Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: sa cāpi śaravarṣaṃ tac charavarṣeṇa vāsaviḥ aprāptam eva ciccheda bhagadattasya vīryavān
english: But the valiant son of Vāsava cut apart with his own rain of arrows that shower of Bhagadatta's shafts even before it could reach him.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāgjyotiṣo rājā śaravarṣaṃ nivārya tat śarair jaghne mahābāhuṃ pārthaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca bhārata
english: Then the king of Prāgjyotiṣa, having warded off that downpour of arrows, struck the mighty-armed Pārtha and Kṛṣṇa with his shafts, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śarajālena mahatābhyavakīrya tau codayām āsa taṃ nāgaṃ vadhāyācyutapārthayoḥ
english: Then, having covered them both with a vast net of arrows, he goaded that elephant on to slay Acyuta and Pārtha.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ dviradaṃ dṛṣṭvā kruddham ivāntakam cakre 'pasavyaṃ tvaritaḥ syandanena janārdanaḥ
english: Seeing that elephant bearing down upon them like wrathful Death itself, Janārdana swiftly wheeled the chariot to keep it on the left.

sanskrit: saṃprāptam api neyeṣa parāvṛttaṃ mahādvipam sārohaṃ mṛtyusāt kartuṃ smaran dharmaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Though the great elephant had now wheeled close, Dhanaṃjaya, mindful of righteousness, did not wish to consign it and its rider to death.

sanskrit: sa tu nāgo dviparathān hayāṃś cārujya māriṣa prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya tato 'krudhyad dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: But that elephant, O lord, crushing other elephants, chariots, and horses, dispatched them to the realm of death; thereupon Dhanaṃjaya grew wrathful.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā kruddhaḥ kim akarod bhagadattasya pāṇḍavaḥ prāgjyotiṣo vā pārthasya tan me śaṃsa yathātatham
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Thus angered, what did the son of Pāṇḍu do to Bhagadatta, or the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa to Pārtha? Tell me that exactly as it befell.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prāgjyotiṣeṇa saṃsaktāv ubhau dāśārhapāṇḍavau mṛtyor ivāntikaṃ prāptau sarvabhūtāni menire
english: Saṃjaya said: When both the Dāśārha and the son of Pāṇḍu were locked in struggle with the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, all creatures believed them brought near to death.

sanskrit: tathā hi śaravarṣāṇi pātayaty aniśaṃ prabho bhagadatto gajaskandhāt kṛṣṇayoḥ syandanasthayoḥ
english: For indeed, O lord, Bhagadatta poured down unceasing showers of arrows from his elephant's shoulders upon the two Kṛṣṇas as they stood upon the chariot.

sanskrit: atha kārṣṇāyasair bāṇaiḥ pūrṇakārmukaniḥsṛtaiḥ avidhyad devakīputraṃ hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Then with shafts of black iron, gold-feathered and whetted on stone, loosed from a fully drawn bow, he pierced the son of Devakī.

sanskrit: agnisparśasamās tīkṣṇā bhagadattena coditāḥ nirbhidya devakīputraṃ kṣitiṃ jagmuḥ śarās tataḥ
english: Sharp as the touch of fire, those arrows, driven by Bhagadatta, pierced through the son of Devakī and then sank into the ground.

sanskrit: tasya pārtho dhanuś chittvā śarāvāpaṃ nihatya ca lāḍayann iva rājānaṃ bhagadattam ayodhayat
english: Pārtha cut his bow, struck down his quiver, and fought King Bhagadatta as though toying with him.

sanskrit: so 'rkaraśminibhāṃs tīkṣṇāṃs tomarān vai caturdaśa prerayat savyasācī tāṃs tridhaikaikam athācchinat
english: He hurled fourteen sharp javelins, bright as the rays of the sun; and Savyasācin cut each of them into three.

sanskrit: tato nāgasya tad varma vyadhamat pākaśāsaniḥ śarajālena sa babhau vyabhraḥ parvatarāḍ iva
english: Then the son of the Chastiser of Pāka tore away the elephant's armor with a net of arrows, so that it shone like a cloudless king of mountains.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāgjyotiṣaḥ śaktiṃ hemadaṇḍām ayasmayīm vyasṛjad vāsudevāya dvidhā tām arjuno 'cchinat
english: Then the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa hurled at Vāsudeva an iron lance with a golden shaft, and Arjuna cut it in two.

sanskrit: tataś chatraṃ dhvajaṃ caiva chittvā rājño 'rjunaḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha daśabhis tūrṇam utsmayan parvatādhipam
english: Then, having cut down the king's parasol and standard with his arrows, Arjuna swiftly pierced the lord of the mountains with ten shafts, smiling the while.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho 'rjunaśaraiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ bhagadattas tataḥ kruddhaḥ pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Deeply pierced by Arjuna's well-feathered shafts winged with heron-plumes, Bhagadatta then, full of wrath against the great-souled son of Pāṇḍu,

sanskrit: vyasṛjat tomarān mūrdhni śvetāśvasyonnanāda ca tair arjunasya samare kirīṭaṃ parivartitam
english: hurled javelins at the head of him whose steeds were white, and roared aloud; and by them Arjuna's diadem was knocked askew in the battle.

sanskrit: parivṛttaṃ kirīṭaṃ taṃ yamayann eva phalgunaḥ sudṛṣṭaḥ kriyatāṃ loka iti rājānam abravīt
english: Setting his displaced diadem aright, Phalguna said to the king, "Take now a good last look at the world."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu saṃkruddhaḥ śaravarṣeṇa pāṇḍavam abhyavarṣat sagovindaṃ dhanur ādāya bhāsvaram
english: Thus addressed, he in great wrath took up his shining bow and rained arrows upon the son of Pāṇḍu together with Govinda.

sanskrit: tasya pārtho dhanuś chittvā tūṇīrān saṃnikṛtya ca tvaramāṇo dvisaptatyā sarvamarmasv atāḍayat
english: Pārtha cut his bow, shattered his quivers, and in haste smote him in all his vital parts with seventy-two arrows.

sanskrit: viddhas tathāpy avyathito vaiṣṇavāstram udīrayan abhimantryāṅkuśaṃ kruddho vyasṛjat pāṇḍavorasi
english: Though so pierced, undismayed, he summoned forth the Vaiṣṇava weapon and, having charged his elephant-goad with mantras, in fury flung it at the breast of the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: visṛṣṭaṃ bhagadattena tad astraṃ sarvaghātakam urasā pratijagrāha pārthaṃ saṃchādya keśavaḥ
english: That all-destroying weapon loosed by Bhagadatta, Keśava received upon his own breast, shielding Pārtha.

sanskrit: vaijayanty abhavan mālā tad astraṃ keśavorasi tato 'rjunaḥ klāntamanāḥ keśavaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Upon Keśava's breast that weapon became a garland of victory; then Arjuna, troubled in mind, said to Keśava:

sanskrit: ayudhyamānas turagān saṃyantāsmi janārdana ity uktvā puṇḍarīkākṣa pratijñāṃ svāṃ na rakṣasi
english: "I am the driver of the horses, taking no part in the fight — so you said, O Janārdana; yet, lotus-eyed one, you do not keep your own vow."

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ vyasanī vā syām aśakto vā nivāraṇe tatas tvayaivaṃ kāryaṃ syān na tu kāryaṃ mayi sthite
english: "Were I in distress, or unable to ward it off, then such a deed would fall to you; but it ought not to be done while I stand firm."

sanskrit: sabāṇaḥ sadhanuś cāhaṃ sasurāsuramānavān śakto lokān imāñ jetuṃ tac cāpi viditaṃ tava
english: "With my arrows and my bow I am able to conquer these worlds with their gods, demons, and men — and this too is known to you."

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ vāsudevaḥ pratyuvācārthavad vacaḥ śṛṇu guhyam idaṃ pārtha yathā vṛttaṃ purānagha
english: Then Vāsudeva answered Arjuna with words full of meaning: "Hear this secret, O sinless Pārtha, even as it came to pass of old."

sanskrit: caturmūrtir ahaṃ śaśval lokatrāṇārtham udyataḥ ātmānaṃ pravibhajyeha lokānāṃ hitam ādadhe
english: "In four forms am I forever exerted for the protection of the worlds; dividing myself here, I take up the welfare of the worlds."

sanskrit: ekā mūrtis tapaścaryāṃ kurute me bhuvi sthitā aparā paśyati jagat kurvāṇaṃ sādhvasādhunī
english: "One of my forms, abiding on earth, performs austerities; another beholds the world doing its deeds, good and evil."

sanskrit: aparā kurute karma mānuṣaṃ lokam āśritā śete caturthī tv aparā nidrāṃ varṣasahasrikām
english: "Another, dwelling in the world of men, performs action; and a fourth lies asleep in a slumber of a thousand years."

sanskrit: yāsau varṣasahasrānte mūrtir uttiṣṭhate mama varārhebhyo varāñ śreṣṭhāṃs tasmin kāle dadāti sā
english: "That form of mine which rises at the close of the thousand years bestows at that time the choicest boons upon those worthy of boons."

sanskrit: taṃ tu kālam anuprāptaṃ viditvā pṛthivī tadā prāyācata varaṃ yaṃ māṃ narakārthāya taṃ śṛṇu
english: "Knowing that time was come, the Earth then begged of me a boon for the sake of Naraka — hear what it was."

sanskrit: devānām asurāṇāṃ ca avadhyas tanayo 'stu me upeto vaiṣṇavāstreṇa tan me tvaṃ dātum arhasi
english: "'Let my son be unslayable by gods and demons alike, endowed with the Vaiṣṇava weapon — this you ought to grant me.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ varam ahaṃ śrutvā jagatyās tanaye tadā amogham astram adadaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tad ahaṃ purā
english: "Hearing that prayer for a boon, I then, of old, gave to the son of the Earth that unfailing Vaiṣṇava weapon."

sanskrit: avocaṃ caitad astraṃ vai hy amoghaṃ bhavatu kṣame narakasyābhirakṣārthaṃ nainaṃ kaś cid vadhiṣyati
english: "And I declared: 'Let this weapon be unfailing and able to bear all; for the protection of Naraka, none shall be able to slay him.'"

sanskrit: anenāstreṇa te guptaḥ sutaḥ parabalārdanaḥ bhaviṣyati durādharṣaḥ sarvalokeṣu sarvadā
english: "'Guarded by this weapon, your son, the crusher of hostile hosts, shall be unassailable in all the worlds for all time.'"

sanskrit: tathety uktvā gatā devī kṛtakāmā manasvinī sa cāpy āsīd durādharṣo narakaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: "Saying 'So be it,' the noble-minded goddess departed, her wish fulfilled; and so Naraka, the tormentor of foes, became unassailable."

sanskrit: tasmāt prāgjyotiṣaṃ prāptaṃ tad astraṃ pārtha māmakam nāsyāvadhyo 'sti lokeṣu sendrarudreṣu māriṣa
english: "From him this weapon of mine has come down to the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, O Pārtha; in the worlds, even with Indra and Rudra, none is beyond its slaying, O lord."

sanskrit: tan mayā tvatkṛtenaitad anyathā vyapanāśitam viyuktaṃ paramāstreṇa jahi pārtha mahāsuram
english: "For your sake I have made it null, disarming it of its supreme power; now, Pārtha, slay that great demon."

sanskrit: vairiṇaṃ yudhi durdharṣaṃ bhagadattaṃ suradviṣam yathāhaṃ jaghnivān pūrvaṃ hitārthaṃ narakaṃ tathā
english: "Slay the foe, hard to vanquish in battle, Bhagadatta, the hater of the gods, even as I formerly slew Naraka for the good of all."

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ pārthaḥ keśavena mahātmanā bhagadattaṃ śitair bāṇaiḥ sahasā samavākirat
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Keśava, Pārtha then suddenly covered Bhagadatta over with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho mahābāhur asaṃbhrānto mahāmanāḥ kumbhayor antare nāgaṃ nārācena samārpayat
english: Then the mighty-armed Pārtha, unflurried and high of heart, struck the elephant between its two frontal globes with an iron shaft.

sanskrit: samāsādya tu taṃ nāgaṃ bāṇo vajra ivācalam abhyagāt saha puṅkhena valmīkam iva pannagaḥ
english: Reaching that elephant, the arrow, like a thunderbolt striking a mountain, sank in up to its feathers, as a serpent enters an anthill.

sanskrit: sa tu viṣṭabhya gātrāṇi dantābhyām avaniṃ yayau nadann ārtasvaraṃ prāṇān utsasarja mahādvipaḥ
english: And that great elephant, bracing its limbs, sank to the earth upon its tusks, and crying out in a voice of anguish, gave up its life.

sanskrit: tataś candrārdhabimbena śareṇa nataparvaṇā bibheda hṛdayaṃ rājño bhagadattasya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then with a straight-jointed arrow shaped like the half-moon's disc, the son of Pāṇḍu pierced the heart of King Bhagadatta.
